metas.name: Agriculture - Banana Plantations
metas.note:
Banana plantations are almost exclusively found in central and southern Mindanao.

NOTE: Wild growing banana plants can be found all over the country, so make sure what you are seeing is an actual plantation before guessing.

metas.name: Agriculture - Corn
metas.note: While corn can be found in most of the country, it is most common on northern Luzon and on Mindanao.

metas.name: Agriculture - Oil
metas.note: The vast majority of Oil palm plantations are found on Mindanao.

metas.name: Agriculture - Pineapple
metas.note: Pineapple plantations are mostly found on Mindanao.

metas.name: Agriculture - Sugarcane
metas.note: The majority of sugarcane in the Philippines can be found on the islands of Negros and Panay.

metas.name: Architecture - Diagonal Amakan
metas.note: Houses built with amakan walls (referred to as Sawali in the north) with a diagonally woven pattern are mostly found on the island of Palawan, but can also be found throughout the northern half of the country.

metas.name: Architecture - Diamond Amakan
metas.note: Houses built with amakan walls, a traditionally woven bamboo mat, with a diamond pattern are almost exclusively found in the southern half of the country.

metas.name: Architecture - Marawi
metas.note: In and around the city of Marawi, Mindanao you can find many destroyed houses and ruins from the Marawi siege in 2017.

metas.name: Car Meta - General Santos Car
metas.note: You may find this black Street View car with a visible roof rack in and around the city of General Santos.

metas.name: Car Meta - Mayon Vehicle
metas.note: This vehicle with several thick black bars can be found just south of the Mayon Volcano.

metas.name: Car Meta - Orange Car
metas.note: An orange Street View car with visible side mirrors can be found on Corregidor Island.

metas.name: Car Meta - Taped Car back
metas.note: In northwestern Bohol you can find this Street View car with tape on the back.

metas.name: Culture -  Mountain Dew Decorations
metas.note: Decorations made of neon-green Mountain Dew bottles are commonly found in the north, particularly on northern Luzon.

metas.name: Culture - Islam
metas.note: While most of the Philippines is strongly christian, a region of western Mindanao is majority muslim.

metas.name: Culture - Roman Soldiers
metas.note: Images and statues of ancient Roman soldiers can be found on the island of Marinduque.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Acne Blocks
metas.note: The southern peninsula of Quezon has these sloped concrete blocks with round spots made from small rocks that kind of look like a skin issue. Blocks in this style with straight edges are common throughout the country, and you can get slanted concrete blocks without the acne in other places as well, but the combination is exclusive to this area.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Philippines by Oliver, who is quoting sleepfor8hx3 on a document that unfortunately is not available at this point in time (2025/04/08)

metas.name: Infrastructure - Bataan Death March
metas.note:
These large decorated white waystones, commemorating the Bataan Death March, can be seen along roads going from Mariveles and Bagac in the south to San Fernando in the north.

NOTE: The Bataan Death March continued from San Fernando to Capas by train, where a larger memorial has been built.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Bicol Stripes
metas.note: White guardrails with three recurring black stripes are unique to the region of Bicol in southern Luzon.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Black & Yellow Guardrail
metas.note: In the Cordillera Administrative Region you can find yellow and black striped concrete guardrails.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Double Pancake Insulator
metas.note: Double pancake insulators are very rare, but most likely to be found along the coast of East Samar, from about the height of the island of Hilabaan all the way down to the southern tip.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Philippines by Oliver & Philippines Poles by vaivod & brikiiee

metas.name: Infrastructure - Indented Pole
metas.note: Square concrete poles with an indent on both side, similar to the poles found in Chile, are mainly found north of Manila and in and around the city of Bacolod on the island of Negros.

metas.name: Infrastructure - K-Waystone
metas.note:
These waystones with K and a number below show the distance related to Manila (or the max distances on specific islands)

This number can be used to narrow down guesses.

For example, certain islands cannot exceed the orange numbers on the image. As another example, Mindanao, and nowhere else, always has numbers above 1000.
metas.footer: Source: philippines km=0 marker by bullfrogggy

metas.name: Infrastructure - Ladder Poletop
metas.note:
A poletop made up of two tall vertical metal bars having an L-shaped cross-section which are connected via several thin wires, making it resemble a ladder, is unique to Manila and the surrounding area.

NOTE: You may sometimes come across similar looking poletops, with square bars instead of L-shaped ones, throughout the entire country. They will however almost never have more than two connecting wires.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Northern Cebu Yellow Blocks
metas.note: In northern Cebu, you will find gray concrete guard blocks with their edges painted yellow.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Philippines by Oliver, who is quoting sleepfor8hx3 on a document that unfortunately is not available at this point in time (2025/04/08)

metas.name: Infrastructure - Northwest-Leyte & Biliran Insulator
metas.note: Three ridges plus a long extender at the top to carry the wire are most commonly found in Leyte and Biliran.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Philippines by Oliver & Philippines Poles by vaivod & brikiiee

metas.name: Infrastructure - Palawan Highway
metas.note:
The highway going south from Puerto Princesa on Palawan can be characterised by being very wide, often featuring six lanes, while simultaneously having very little traffic.

Along the road you will usually see this double electrical wire, which can help confirm your guess.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Quad Insulator
metas.note: This cylinder with four distinct ridges is most common in Ilocos Norte, but can also be found in Biliran.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Philippines by Oliver & Philippines Poles by vaivod & brikiiee

metas.name: Infrastructure - Quad Pancake Insulator
metas.note: If you see a quadruple pancake insulator on a pole top, you're going to be on the one road with coverage in Davao Occidental, along the coast, between approximately Don Marcelino and Bukid.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Philippines by Oliver & Philippines Poles by vaivod & brikiiee

metas.name: Infrastructure - Sausage Insulator
metas.note: This grey insulator with lots of small ridges that looks kind of solid is most common in and around Manila, but can rarely be found elsewhere.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Philippines by Oliver & Philippines Poles by vaivod & brikiiee

metas.name: Infrastructure - Siquijor Lamp
metas.note: Lamp posts on Siquijor are typically painted yellow, with black stripes at the bottom.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Square Metal Mesh Poles
metas.note:
Square metal mesh poles are found on Mindanao, mainly on the Zamboanga peninsula.

NOTE: Most of the poles found outside of the Zamboanga peninsula are found along highways and have poletops with three hanging insulators.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Star Wars Insulator
metas.note: This type of insulator that looks like the buildings on Tatooine is most common in northern Luzon and in and around Manila.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Philippines by Oliver & Philippines Poles by vaivod & brikiiee

metas.name: Infrastructure - Trike - Dipolog City
metas.note:
The Zamboanga Peninsula trike is recognizable through the passenger window shape (airplane window). Other notables parts are the roof leaning back, and the trike kinda bulging out from under the window. Some cities have specific variants of this Trike:

Dipolog City likes to have the tiniest window imaginable over the driver’s side of the car & a big number on the roof.
metas.footer: Source: A Comprehensive Guide to Filipino Trikes by vaivod

metas.name: Infrastructure - Trike - Isulan
metas.note: These trikes with the large flat black roof, the small side window and no lines in the main window are found in Sultan Kudarat mainly. These green trikes with blue POBLACION text on them are specific to Isulan.
metas.footer: Source: A Comprehensive Guide to Filipino Trikes by vaivod

metas.name: Infrastructure - Trike - Ozamiz City
metas.note:
The Zamboanga Peninsula trike is recognizable through the passenger window shape (airplane window). Other notables parts are the roof leaning back, and the trike kinda bulging out from under the window. Some cities have specific variants of this Trike:

One city-specific variant to note is this one, with these bubbly numbers on top of the driver’s window (the trike itself can be any color scheme), which are exclusive to Ozamiz City and surrounding areas.
metas.footer: Source: A Comprehensive Guide to Filipino Trikes by vaivod

metas.name: Infrastructure - Trike - Square Roof
metas.note: These trikes with a square roof are also very common within Maguindanao.
metas.footer: Source: A Comprehensive Guide to Filipino Trikes by vaivod

metas.name: Infrastructure - Trike - Sultan Kudarat
metas.note: These trikes with the large flat black roof, the small side window and no lines in the main window are found in Sultan Kudarat mainly.
metas.footer: Source: A Comprehensive Guide to Filipino Trikes by vaivod

metas.name: Infrastructure - Trike - Tacurong City
metas.note: These trikes with the large flat black roof, the small side window and no lines in the main window are found in Sultan Kudarat mainly. This more colorful variant with a number on top is specific to Tacurong City.
metas.footer: Source: A Comprehensive Guide to Filipino Trikes by vaivod

metas.name: Infrastructure - Trike - Umbrella
metas.note:
These trikes with an umbrella are super common in Maguindanao, Misamis Occidental, and Lanao del Sur. Note that these are really the only trikes found in Cotabato city, so if there’s only these guys it’s a good clue for there.

NOTE: These are also very common in Cebu!
metas.footer: Source: A Comprehensive Guide to Filipino Trikes by vaivod

metas.name: Infrastructure - Trike - Zamboanga City
metas.note:
The Zamboanga Peninsula trike is recognizable through the passenger window shape (airplane window). Other notables parts are the roof leaning back, and the trike kinda bulging out from under the window. Some cities have specific variants of this Trike:

This trike is a Zamboanga city trike- they have a flat roof, a white line separating the passenger and the driver’s side. There’s a little bumper thing jutting out from under the window, and there’s still the vertical bit underneath the passenger’s window. Zamboanga city specifically has these super colorful trikes.

This type of trike is still identifiable from the back due to the black cloth roof, the large window with the singular white line, and the back having a side window. These less colorful variants can be found Northeast of the main city.
metas.footer: Source: A Comprehensive Guide to Filipino Trikes by vaivod

metas.name: Infrastructure - Trike - Zamboanga City (non-colorful variant)
metas.note:
The Zamboanga Peninsula trike is recognizable through the passenger window shape (airplane window). Other notables parts are the roof leaning back, and the trike kinda bulging out from under the window. Some cities have specific variants of this Trike:

This trike is a Zamboanga city trike- they have a flat roof, a white line separating the passenger and the driver’s side. There’s a little bumper thing jutting out from under the window, and there’s still the vertical bit underneath the passenger’s window. Zamboanga city specifically has these super colorful trikes.

This type of trike is still identifiable from the back due to the black cloth roof, the large window with the singular white line, and the back having a side window. These less colorful variants can be found Northeast of the main city.
metas.footer: Source: A Comprehensive Guide to Filipino Trikes by vaivod

metas.name: Infrastructure - Trike - Zamboanga Peninsula
metas.note:
This trike shape is essentially the only variant seen on the entire Zamboanga Peninsula. What sticks out to me is the passenger window shape- it’s kind of like an airplane window. Other notable parts are the roof leaning back, and the trike kinda bulging out from under the window.

It’s identifiable from the back as well from the singular window in the back, as well as the roof tilting, and the random bars on top.

A common variant is this one with a large window hanging over the driver’s side. You can tell it’s the same type of trike from the same shape of the passenger car- where it has the airplane window (even if it’s horizontal) and then the bit beneath it that’s completely vertical and flat, along with the roof tilting back.
metas.footer: Source: A Comprehensive Guide to Filipino Trikes by vaivod

metas.name: Infrastructure - Yellow Backboards
metas.note: On the islands of Panay and Guimaras (the little island next to Iloilo), electricity counters are frequently mounted on yellow backboards. These can be horizontal or vertical, metal or wood.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Philippines by Oliver, who is quoting sleepfor8hx3 on a document that unfortunately is not available at this point in time (2025/04/08)

metas.name: Landscape - Arayat Volcano
metas.note: The Arayat Volcano can be recognised by being completely surrounded by flat agricultural fields.

metas.name: Landscape - Chocolate Hills
metas.note: On central Bohol you can find these distinct round grassy hills. The hills generally have dark brown soil beneath the grass, earning them the name of Chocolate Hills.

metas.name: Landscape - Mayon Volcano
metas.note: The Mayon Volcano is one of the tallest mountains in the Philippines and can be recognised by its almost perfect smooth cone shape. Beware that it will very often be covered in clouds.

metas.name: Landscape - Northern Luzon Landscape
metas.note: The forested mountain range in Northern Luzon is characterised by somewhat dry mountainsides and an abundance of pine trees. You may rarely come across a similar landscape on high-altitude roads in Mindanao.

metas.name: Vegetation - Moluccan Albizia
metas.note: Moluccan albizia are trees with light coloured trunks and pinnate leaves near the top of the tree. They are mainly found on Mindanao and are especially common in the eastern and central regions of the island.

metas.name: Vehicle - Crown Roof Tuk-Tuk
metas.note: Tuk-Tuks with a crown roof can be found mostly in Northern Luzon. The crown consists of two separate parts, a "rectangular" part and a "crown-shaped" part. Some Tuk-Tuks elsewhere will have a wavy top, but are not made of two parts and thus are not crowns.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & A Learnable Philippines by Oliver

metas.name: Vehicle - Flat Roof Tuk-Tuk
metas.note: Flat roofs are mostly found in the south. If it's a three-wheeler (as seen on the leftmost), you're probably on Mindanao.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & A Learnable Philippines by Oliver

metas.name: Vehicle - Kuliglig
metas.note: This type of tractor, called a kuliglig, is mostly found on the plains around Cauayan on northern Luzon.

metas.name: Vehicle - Low Roof Tuk-Tuk
metas.note: Low roof Tuk-Tuks are generally found in the North.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & A Learnable Philippines by Oliver

metas.name: Vehicle - Motorcycle Plate Meta
metas.note:
If a Motorcycle plate has a colorful stripe on it, you can use it to determine the region you're in.

In general, if the stripe is on the top, you're in the Northern half.

If it's on the bottom, you're in the Southern half
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & A Learnable Philippines by Oliver

metas.name: Vehicle - Palawan Tuk Tuk
metas.note: This Tuk-Tuk with a single front window and flat roof is exclusive to Palawan.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & A Learnable Philippines by Oliver
